The numerical work is organized into **thirteen experiment notebooks**:
four positive-shift studies, four mean-zero zero-shift studies, four
added-mean zero-shift studies, and one separate single-mode
nonzero-mean benchmark. Each experiment has explicit parameters and a
manual computation chunk. Knitting reads saved results and redraws figures;
missing or incompatible results stop with a manual-run instruction.

[Positive-shift theory and functions](brasilfunc.html) ·
[Zero-shift theory and functions](kappa0func.html) ·
[Positive-shift combined figure](about.html#rational-and-spatial-convergence)

## Original positive-shift convergence studies: kappa = 4

These are the original mean-zero experiments reported in the manuscript.
Their source notebooks are unchanged.

- [Isolated convergence in rational order](conv_in_m_isolated.html).
- [Smooth spatial convergence](cov_in_h_mat.html).
- [Smooth temporal convergence](conv_in_tau_mat.html).
- [Rough spatial convergence](cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.html).

## Additional zero-shift BRASIL studies: kappa = 0

These retain the original convergence data and error definitions with the
unshifted operator, exact mean handling, and a positive gap scale of 1/3.
The initial and forcing means remain zero. Numerical parameter adjustments
are stated in the relevant notebook.

- [Isolated convergence in rational order](true_diff_conv_in_m_isolated.html).
- [Smooth spatial convergence](true_diff_cov_in_h_mat.html).
- [Smooth temporal convergence](true_diff_conv_in_tau_mat.html).
- [Rough spatial convergence](true_diff_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.html).

## Added-mean zero-shift convergence studies

These use initial and forcing means both equal to 1. The m and time
studies retain their audited archived settings; the two spatial studies
use finer time grids and higher rational orders to reduce nuisance errors. Their centered diffusion is unchanged: the
solution
is the corresponding mean-zero solution plus 1+t, and its mass is 3(1+t).
They have separate result and figure paths. Earlier restored results
remain available. The rough counterpart computes its own centered run
plus the exact constant mode; it was not an archived added-mean run.
Every study includes all nine fractional exponents.

- [Isolated convergence in rational order, nonzero mean](nonzero_mean_conv_in_m_isolated.html).
- [Smooth spatial convergence, nonzero mean](nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_mat.html).
- [Smooth temporal convergence, nonzero mean](nonzero_mean_conv_in_tau_mat.html).
- [Rough spatial convergence, nonzero mean](nonzero_mean_cov_in_h_rough_as_in_mat.html).

## Separate nonzero-mean zero-shift benchmark

[Zero-shift benchmark](true_diff_zero_shift_benchmark.html) contains:

1. The manuscript's exact-discrete spectral FEM spatial and temporal benchmark.
2. An additional BRASIL comparison on the same nonzero-mean data, including mass balance.
3. The manuscript's small-shift spectral comparison at kappa = 0, 0.0001, and 0.01.

The single-mode nonzero-mean benchmark is separate from the convergence studies above.
Internal implementation tests and refinement audits are kept in
`/home/rierasl/Desktop/DOCS/NAP/true_diff_internal`; they do not execute
when any of these thirteen reports is knitted.
